_about.purpose: EditForge's vocabulary. Every editing technique we know exists, what it looks like, what SIGNAL it leaves in the pixels, and whether we can therefore detect it. This is what Claude classifies a reference video against, and what the tool reports honestly when it sees something it cannot reproduce.

status_values.built: a detector exists and is verified against ground truth
status_values.buildable: leaves a real, measurable signal; a detector could be written and verified
status_values.nameable: a vision model can identify it, but we cannot cleanly measure its parameters — report it, do not fake it
status_values.impossible: the information is destroyed by rendering. No detector can ever recover it. Do not let this list shrink through optimism.

_about.signal: The measurable fingerprint. This field, not the name, is what decides if detection is possible.
_about.prevalence_warning: prevalence is MY ESTIMATE. Deep research (2026-07-12) specifically REFUTED the web sources that rank transition popularity in short-form — they were SEO/vendor blogs with no independent corroboration. Treat these as priors to test, not facts.
_about.sourcing_note: The film-grammar and After Effects mechanics below verified strongly in research (3-0 votes). The creator/short-form slang layer did NOT verify — the techniques are real, but their names and popularity rankings come from unreliable sources. Names may vary.

cuts_and_transitions.name: Hard cut
cuts_and_transitions.looks_like: Instant switch, no blend frames.
cuts_and_transitions.ae: Adjacent layers, no overlap.
cuts_and_transitions.signal: Content discontinuity with NO intermediate frames; sharpness does not dip.

cuts_and_transitions.name: Cross dissolve
cuts_and_transitions.looks_like: Outgoing shot fades out as incoming fades in; both briefly superimposed.
cuts_and_transitions.ae: Opacity ramp on overlapping layers.
cuts_and_transitions.signal: Frames are literal linear blends of A and B. Blend weight ramps 0->1 THROUGH the middle. Sharpness DIPS to ~0.5x (averaging uncorrelated detail destroys it) — this is the reliable discriminator, not the blend residual.

cuts_and_transitions.name: Fade to/from black
cuts_and_transitions.looks_like: Image sinks to black and returns.
cuts_and_transitions.ae: Opacity ramp, or a black solid above.
cuts_and_transitions.signal: Luminance collapses toward zero and recovers.

cuts_and_transitions.name: Dip to white
cuts_and_transitions.looks_like: Image blows out to white and returns.
cuts_and_transitions.ae: White solid, opacity ramp.
cuts_and_transitions.signal: Luminance spikes toward max across the boundary.
cuts_and_transitions.note: Our flash detector covers this; 'wash' is the film term for a fade through any solid colour.

cuts_and_transitions.name: Flash cut / light leak
cuts_and_transitions.looks_like: One-to-three frame bright pop at the cut.
cuts_and_transitions.ae: White/warm solid, short opacity spike; or a light-leak clip in Screen mode.
cuts_and_transitions.signal: Luminance spike far above the shot's own median, lasting a few frames.

cuts_and_transitions.name: Whip pan
cuts_and_transitions.looks_like: Camera flies sideways, everything smears, lands on a new shot.
cuts_and_transitions.ae: Directional Blur + fast Position keys; or in-camera.
cuts_and_transitions.signal: MOTION plus blur. Huge frame displacement (phase correlation) AND sharpness collapse. Blur alone is NOT enough — it is indistinguishable from a dissolve. Direction and speed must match across the cut for the illusion to work.

cuts_and_transitions.name: J-cut
cuts_and_transitions.looks_like: You HEAR the next scene before you SEE it.
cuts_and_transitions.ae: Offset the audio layer earlier than the picture.
cuts_and_transitions.signal: Requires per-shot audio source separation — we would need to know which audio belongs to which shot. Not recoverable from a single mixed track.
cuts_and_transitions.prevalence: common in narrative, rare in short-form
cuts_and_transitions.note: Verified 3-0. A split edit, not a picture transition. Only meaningful with separate audio stems.

cuts_and_transitions.name: L-cut
cuts_and_transitions.looks_like: The outgoing shot's sound carries over the incoming picture.
cuts_and_transitions.ae: Extend the audio layer past the picture cut.
cuts_and_transitions.signal: Same problem as the J-cut — needs stems.
cuts_and_transitions.prevalence: common in narrative, rare in short-form

cuts_and_transitions.name: Directional wipe
cuts_and_transitions.looks_like: A hard edge sweeps across, replacing one shot with another.
cuts_and_transitions.ae: Linear Wipe effect.
cuts_and_transitions.signal: A moving boundary: one side is shot A, the other shot B, with a travelling edge. Detectable by segmenting the frame at a straight moving edge.

cuts_and_transitions.name: Iris / clock wipe
cuts_and_transitions.looks_like: A circle or sweeping radial hand reveals the next shot.
cuts_and_transitions.ae: Radial Wipe / Iris Wipe / CC Grid Wipe.
cuts_and_transitions.signal: A growing circular or angular boundary between two shots.

cuts_and_transitions.name: Shape / graphic wipe
cuts_and_transitions.looks_like: A shape grows and reveals the next shot.
cuts_and_transitions.ae: Mask on the incoming layer, animated.
cuts_and_transitions.signal: A boundary matching a known shape template.

cuts_and_transitions.name: Luma / gradient wipe
cuts_and_transitions.looks_like: The next shot bleeds in through an irregular texture (ink, smoke, paint).
cuts_and_transitions.ae: Gradient Wipe driven by a greyscale matte.
cuts_and_transitions.signal: Per-pixel reveal ordered by an arbitrary greyscale image. The reveal ORDER is recoverable (which pixels switch when), but the matte itself is an arbitrary image we would have to reconstruct.
cuts_and_transitions.note: Verified 3-0 that this is a real wipe sibling. Partially detectable: we can see a non-geometric reveal is happening, which is enough to STOP calling it a hard cut.

cuts_and_transitions.name: Zoom transition
cuts_and_transitions.looks_like: Shot rushes toward camera, blurs, lands on the next shot.
cuts_and_transitions.ae: Scale keys + Radial (Zoom) Blur.
cuts_and_transitions.signal: Rapid scale ramp across the cut plus radial blur centred on frame centre. Distinguishable from a whip by blur GEOMETRY: radial vs directional.

cuts_and_transitions.name: Spin transition
cuts_and_transitions.looks_like: Frame whips around its centre into the next shot.
cuts_and_transitions.ae: Rotation keys + directional/radial blur.
cuts_and_transitions.signal: Large rotation across the boundary (our similarity transform already measures rotation) plus blur.
cuts_and_transitions.note: Our motion tracker already recovers roll — this is mostly wiring.

cuts_and_transitions.name: Glitch transition
cuts_and_transitions.looks_like: Frame tears, blocks, colour-shifts, static, for a few frames.
cuts_and_transitions.ae: Plugin stacks; or Displacement Map + channel offsets + noise.
cuts_and_transitions.signal: A few frames of high-frequency noise, block artifacts, and channel misalignment. Very detectable AS AN ANOMALY (frames that match neither shot), even if the exact look is not reproducible.

cuts_and_transitions.name: Datamosh
cuts_and_transitions.looks_like: One shot's motion vectors smear into the next; pixels melt.
cuts_and_transitions.ae: Not a normal effect — done by deleting I-frames in the encoded stream.
cuts_and_transitions.signal: Highly distinctive: content changes while motion vectors persist. Detectable as an anomaly. Reproducing it requires bitstream manipulation, not an AE effect.

cuts_and_transitions.name: Morph cut
cuts_and_transitions.looks_like: Two shots blend so smoothly you cannot see the join.
cuts_and_transitions.ae: Premiere's Morph Cut (a speech-gap repair tool) — different from an optical morph.
cuts_and_transitions.signal: By DESIGN leaves minimal signal. If it worked, our cut detector never fires. We would miss it entirely and never know.
cuts_and_transitions.note: The honest failure mode: a perfect invisible cut is, to us, not a cut.

cuts_and_transitions.name: Match cut
cuts_and_transitions.looks_like: A cut where shape/motion/composition carries across, so it feels continuous.
cuts_and_transitions.ae: Not an effect — a shot-selection decision.
cuts_and_transitions.signal: Detectable as a cut with unusually high visual similarity across the boundary. But it is a CONTENT choice, and we cannot reproduce it without matching content — which Julian explicitly does not want.

cuts_and_transitions.name: Jump cut
cuts_and_transitions.looks_like: Same framing, time skips forward. Subject jumps position.
cuts_and_transitions.ae: Cut within one continuous shot.
cuts_and_transitions.signal: Cut with near-identical background/framing but a discontinuous subject. Detectable: background stays, foreground jumps.

cuts_and_transitions.name: Smash cut
cuts_and_transitions.looks_like: Abrupt cut between wildly contrasting shots/energy, usually on a sound hit.
cuts_and_transitions.ae: A hard cut, chosen for contrast.
cuts_and_transitions.signal: A hard cut with a large energy/luminance/audio discontinuity. We can detect the discontinuity; 'smash cut' is an interpretation of it.

time_manipulation.name: Velocity edit
time_manipulation.looks_like: Speed rushes through the dull part of a shot and SLAMS into slow motion on the beat. Changes land on the music.
time_manipulation.ae: Time Remapping with eased keys (NOT Time Stretch — that is constant-rate only), + optical-flow interpolation (Twixtor) to smooth the slow part.
time_manipulation.signal: DETECTABLE, and this is the single most valuable thing to build. Global apparent-motion magnitude (which motion.py already computes per frame) changes WITHIN a shot with no cut. Crucially: because we retime the USER'S clip, we never need the reference's ABSOLUTE speed — only its RELATIVE speed curve, and relative is exactly what is measurable. Residual ambiguity: a subject genuinely accelerating looks the same as a retime. Accept it — copying the apparent-speed rhythm is the goal anyway.
time_manipulation.prevalence: THE defining move of the genre
time_manipulation.note: Verified 3-0 across BOTH research passes. CapCut exposes it as Speed > Curve (0.1x-10x) with six named presets (Montage, Hero, Bullet, Jump Cut, Flash In, Flash Out) and beat markers as alignment anchors.

time_manipulation.name: Optical-flow interpolation
time_manipulation.looks_like: Slow motion that is smooth rather than juddery or ghosted.
time_manipulation.ae: Twixtor (RE:Vision, ~$330 — packs ship SETTINGS presets, never the plugin). AI interpolators (RIFE/Flowframes) are increasingly used as a pre-render step.
time_manipulation.signal: DETECTABLE BY ITS ARTIFACTS. It SYNTHESISES new frames by per-pixel motion estimation, and its unavoidable failure mode is WARPING/MELTING — limbs smearing into backgrounds, faces distorting. That warp is a measurable non-rigid distortion. Distinct from Frame Mix, which ghosts/double-exposes instead.
time_manipulation.prevalence: canonical — the scene's generic verb for interpolation
time_manipulation.note: The #1 practitioner tell of an AMATEUR edit is visible warping here. Detecting it would let us tell Julian how well the reference was made, not just what it did.

time_manipulation.name: Slow motion (uniform)
time_manipulation.looks_like: Everything moves slowly, at a constant rate.
time_manipulation.ae: Time Stretch (constant rate) + Frame Mix or Pixel Motion blending.
time_manipulation.signal: NONE, for the pure case: 60fps footage played at 30 and 30fps footage slowed to 0.5x are PIXEL-IDENTICAL. No measurement separates them. BUT READ THE NOTE — this entry is narrower than it looks.
time_manipulation.note: SCOPE CORRECTION (research pass 2): this 'impossible' verdict applies ONLY to UNIFORM slow-mo of natively high-fps footage. It does NOT apply to (a) speed RAMPS — see velocity_edit, fully detectable — nor (b) INTERPOLATED slow-mo, which leaves warping artifacts — see twixtor. Earlier sessions over-generalised this into 'all speed manipulation is impossible', which is FALSE and was blocking the genre's core technique. Still do not invent uniform slow-mo as a preset: it stretches shot durations and corrupts the rhythm we exist to copy.

time_manipulation.name: Freeze frame
time_manipulation.looks_like: Motion stops dead; one frame holds.
time_manipulation.ae: Time Remap with a hold keyframe (Freeze Frame).
time_manipulation.signal: Frame-to-frame difference collapses to ~zero for several frames.
time_manipulation.note: DETECTED but not yet applied in AE. Risk: a locked-off shot of a still subject false-positives. Validate on real footage first.

time_manipulation.name: Stutter / strobe
time_manipulation.looks_like: Motion becomes choppy, snapping between held frames.
time_manipulation.ae: Posterize Time, or repeated hold keys on Time Remap.
time_manipulation.signal: Frame difference alternates between ~zero and large, in a regular period. Very distinctive.

time_manipulation.name: Reverse
time_manipulation.signal: Hard to detect from pixels alone in general, though physical cues (falling objects rising, smoke retracting) exist. Not reliably measurable.

time_manipulation.name: Timelapse / hyperlapse
time_manipulation.looks_like: Time rushes; clouds race, crowds blur.
time_manipulation.signal: Same ambiguity as slow-mo in the general case, but extreme cases are inferable from implausible motion rates.

time_manipulation.name: Frame blending
time_manipulation.looks_like: Retimed footage looks smooth rather than juddery.
time_manipulation.ae: Two modes, verified: Frame Mix (crossfades adjacent frames) and Pixel Motion (synthesises new frames from tracked motion).
time_manipulation.signal: Ghosting/interpolation artifacts on retimed footage. Detectable as an artifact, but it is a PROPERTY of a retime, not an edit in itself.
time_manipulation.prevalence: common (as a setting, not a choice)

camera_and_motion.name: Push in / pull out
camera_and_motion.looks_like: Frame closes on or retreats from the subject.

camera_and_motion.name: Handheld shake
camera_and_motion.ae: Wiggle expression on Position, or measured keys.
camera_and_motion.signal: High-frequency, low-amplitude translation — falls straight out of the motion track.

camera_and_motion.name: Shake on the beat
camera_and_motion.looks_like: Sharp jolt of the frame exactly on a music hit.
camera_and_motion.ae: Position/Scale keys, or an audio-amplitude-driven expression.
camera_and_motion.signal: Motion spike correlated with a detected beat. We measure both motion AND beats — this is a correlation we simply do not compute yet.
camera_and_motion.note: Cheap win: we already have both halves.

camera_and_motion.name: Zoom punch on beat
camera_and_motion.looks_like: Quick scale pop on the beat, settling back.
camera_and_motion.signal: Scale spike correlated with a beat.
camera_and_motion.note: Previously a FAKE preset; now covered by real measured camera motion. Do not reintroduce it as a rule.

camera_and_motion.name: Parallax / 2.5D
camera_and_motion.looks_like: Foreground and background move at different rates, faking depth.
camera_and_motion.signal: Optical flow field that is NOT a single global transform — it splits by depth. Our RANSAC deliberately discards this as outliers. Detectable in principle by segmenting the flow field.

camera_and_motion.name: Motion tracking
camera_and_motion.looks_like: A graphic or effect sticks to a moving object.
camera_and_motion.ae: Tracker / Mocha, parented to a null.
camera_and_motion.signal: Requires detecting the overlay AND its attachment to an object. Compound problem.

distortion_and_stylisation.name: RGB split
distortion_and_stylisation.looks_like: Red and blue channels offset from each other; coloured edges.
distortion_and_stylisation.signal: STRONG and easy: cross-correlate the R and B channels for a sub-pixel spatial offset. A clean video has none.
distortion_and_stylisation.note: Highest value-to-effort ratio of anything unbuilt.

distortion_and_stylisation.name: Glitch / digital artifacting
distortion_and_stylisation.signal: Anomalous high-frequency structure inconsistent with the surrounding frames.

distortion_and_stylisation.name: VHS / retro look
distortion_and_stylisation.looks_like: Scanlines, chroma bleed, tracking noise, date stamp.
distortion_and_stylisation.ae: Effect stack: noise, chroma shift, scanline overlay.
distortion_and_stylisation.signal: Compound: horizontal banding + chroma bleed + grain. Each component measurable.

distortion_and_stylisation.name: Radial / zoom blur
distortion_and_stylisation.signal: Blur whose direction is radial from a centre point — measurable by comparing gradient energy radially vs tangentially.

distortion_and_stylisation.name: Motion blur
distortion_and_stylisation.looks_like: Moving things smear along their direction of travel.
distortion_and_stylisation.ae: Layer motion blur; Directional Blur; RSMB (RE:Vision) added AFTER a retime.
distortion_and_stylisation.signal: Anisotropic blur aligned with the motion vector.
distortion_and_stylisation.note: OPEN HYPOTHESIS, NOT A FINDING. Research pass 2 tried and FAILED to establish that RSMB is 'near-universal / always bundled with Twixtor' — every pack-level claim was REFUTED. What IS established: the retiming vendor prescribes adding motion blur after Twixtor, and the clean-vs-amateur source rule is to shoot the SHORTEST shutter (no baked-in blur, which smears the pixel correspondences optical flow needs) and add blur back afterwards. Do not build on the universality assumption.

distortion_and_stylisation.name: Ripple / wave warp
distortion_and_stylisation.ae: Wave Warp, Turbulent Displace, Displacement Map.
distortion_and_stylisation.signal: A smooth, periodic, non-rigid displacement field — optical flow that is locally smooth but NOT a global similarity transform. Detectable as 'flow that our rigid model cannot explain'.
distortion_and_stylisation.note: Julian specifically asked about this one. It is detectable as a residual against our rigid motion model — that residual is exactly what we currently throw away as RANSAC outliers.

distortion_and_stylisation.name: Lens distortion
distortion_and_stylisation.signal: Radially symmetric geometric distortion — straight lines curve.

distortion_and_stylisation.name: Mirror / kaleidoscope
distortion_and_stylisation.looks_like: Frame reflected about an axis, or repeated radially.
distortion_and_stylisation.signal: Very detectable: the frame correlates strongly with its own reflection.

distortion_and_stylisation.name: Pixel sorting
distortion_and_stylisation.looks_like: Rows/columns of pixels streak and sort by brightness.

colour_and_look.name: Colour grade
colour_and_look.looks_like: Overall colour/contrast character of the image.
colour_and_look.signal: Global colour statistics. Measurable — but our current implementation (global mean/std match in LAB, Reinhard) LOOKS BAD because it smears the whole image toward the reference's average. A lift/gamma/gain fit or histogram match is the right approach.
colour_and_look.note: CURRENTLY DISABLED at Julian's request — 'it looks bad'. The signal is real; the algorithm is wrong.

colour_and_look.name: Film grain / noise
colour_and_look.looks_like: Fine moving texture over the image.
colour_and_look.signal: High-frequency energy that is temporally uncorrelated. Easy to measure.

colour_and_look.name: Vignette
colour_and_look.ae: Lumetri vignette, or a radial mask.
colour_and_look.signal: Radial luminance falloff from centre to corners. Trivially measurable.

colour_and_look.name: Bloom / glow / halation
colour_and_look.looks_like: Highlights bleed light into surrounding areas.
colour_and_look.signal: Light spill around highlights — measurable by comparing highlight neighbourhoods against a clean model. Weak signal, entangled with content.

colour_and_look.name: Light leak
colour_and_look.looks_like: Warm coloured wash bleeding across frame, often at cuts.
colour_and_look.signal: Additive coloured gradient uncorrelated with content. Detectable at cuts as a coloured luminance spike (our flash detector partially catches this).

colour_and_look.name: Duotone / colour isolation
colour_and_look.looks_like: Image mapped to two colours, or one colour kept and the rest desaturated.
colour_and_look.signal: The colour histogram collapses onto a line or a narrow hue band. Very measurable.

colour_and_look.name: Film emulation
colour_and_look.looks_like: Specific colour response, grain, halation, highlight rolloff.
colour_and_look.signal: A compound of grade + grain + bloom. Identifiable as a look; not separable into a unique recipe.

overlays_and_graphics.name: Captions / subtitles
overlays_and_graphics.looks_like: Text, usually centred or lower third, often word-by-word on the beat.
overlays_and_graphics.signal: Text detection + OCR gives position, timing, and content. Very achievable with EAST/Tesseract.
overlays_and_graphics.note: One of the most visible things we currently ignore completely.

overlays_and_graphics.name: Kinetic typography
overlays_and_graphics.looks_like: Text scales/slides/pops, usually on the beat.
overlays_and_graphics.signal: OCR + tracking the text bounding box over time.

overlays_and_graphics.name: Letterbox / aspect framing
overlays_and_graphics.signal: Constant black rows/columns at frame edges. TRIVIAL to detect.
overlays_and_graphics.note: Embarrassingly easy and we do not do it.

overlays_and_graphics.name: Split screen
overlays_and_graphics.looks_like: Frame divided into regions showing different footage.
overlays_and_graphics.signal: Frame partitions with independent motion/content per region. Detectable via flow-field segmentation.

overlays_and_graphics.name: Picture-in-picture
overlays_and_graphics.looks_like: A smaller frame inset over the main one.
overlays_and_graphics.signal: A rectangular/elliptical region whose content is independent of the background.

overlays_and_graphics.name: Stickers / emoji / memes
overlays_and_graphics.looks_like: Graphic elements pasted over the video.
overlays_and_graphics.signal: Regions that are temporally static and inconsistent with the underlying motion field. Detectable as 'this region does not move with the scene'.

overlays_and_graphics.name: Progress bar
overlays_and_graphics.looks_like: A bar filling across the frame edge.
overlays_and_graphics.signal: A thin region with a monotonically advancing boundary.

audio_driven.name: Cutting on the beat
audio_driven.looks_like: Cuts land on the music's pulse.
audio_driven.signal: Correlation between cut times and detected beats.

audio_driven.name: Transition on the drop
audio_driven.looks_like: The biggest transition lands on the track's drop.
audio_driven.signal: Audio energy/onset spike correlated with a transition. We detect beats but not DROPS (a different, coarser feature — sudden sustained energy rise).

audio_driven.name: Audio-reactive scale/shake
audio_driven.looks_like: The frame pulses in time with the bass.
audio_driven.ae: Convert Audio to Keyframes -> expression on Scale/Position.
audio_driven.signal: Correlation between an audio amplitude envelope and measured frame motion. We have both signals already.

audio_driven.name: SFX punctuation
audio_driven.signal: Detectable as audio onsets at cut points — but it is an AUDIO edit, and we do not reproduce the reference's audio (not Julian's to publish).

styles.name: Velocity / phonk edit
styles.looks_like: Aggressive speed ramps on the beat, heavy shake, RGB split, high contrast grade, fast cuts.

styles.name: AMV / anime edit
styles.looks_like: Beat-synced cuts, zoom punches, glow, chromatic aberration, text pops, dramatic grade.

styles.name: MTV-style fast cutting
styles.looks_like: Very short shots, high energy, jump cuts, whip pans.

styles.name: Vlog style
styles.looks_like: Jump cuts on speech, captions, handheld, occasional whip transitions, music bed.

styles.name: Talking head / educational
styles.looks_like: Jump cuts to remove pauses, burned-in captions, zoom punches for emphasis, b-roll inserts.

styles.name: Sports hype edit
styles.looks_like: Speed ramps into impacts, freeze frames, heavy grade, shake, flash cuts.

styles.name: ASMR / satisfying
styles.looks_like: Long unbroken takes, minimal cuts, close framing, no music-driven cutting.
styles.note: Notable as the ANTI-pattern: almost no edit signal to copy.

styles.name: Cinematic / travel montage
styles.looks_like: Slow push-ins, dissolves, letterboxing, film grade, speed ramps, music-led.
